Why GPUs plateau. A GPU's per-user rate is bounded twice: by the bandwidth roof of the devices serving the user (tokens/s <= bandwidth / bytes per token) and by a synchronisation ceiling that more devices cannot raise. On one B200, the Qwen3-8B modeled 8K roof is 457 tok/s at BF16; the cited 230-tok/s application point has no verified 8K context match. Spreading it over an NVL72 slice (TP8, the largest split its 8 KV heads allow) raises the roof eightfold but adds 73 dependent all-reduces, so the idealised rate stops at 2,241. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash never reaches its roof on GPUs under the modeled collective graph: its 209 collectives per token at the best measured GB200 kernel (2.37 us) cap it near 2,019 tok/s however many GPUs are added (1,879 on 50 B200s, 1,920 on all 72 of an NVL72; 3,029 even at the speed-of-light collective floor). The specialised HBM accelerator raises the synchronisation ceiling, not the roof: with compiled handoffs (4.8 ns on chip against 1.0 us) and in-switch reduction it reaches 3,580 tok/s on V4.1 at roughly matched HBM bandwidth (346 against 360 TB/s), 1.91x the best-kernel GPU; on a single die at the same modeled bandwidth roof, this model assigns no added rate to the specialised HBM core (1.00x on Qwen3-8B). ROM removes the weight term: the design leaves the weights-plus-KV roof for the KV-only roof, 8,941 tok/s on six stacks for Qwen3-8B at 8K, where the ROM reticle sits (8,910, 4.8x the same core streaming 3.5-bit weights at the B200's bandwidth); for V4.1 it is bound by its compiled chain and reaches 8,185 tok/s, 2.3x the equal-area HBM array (23,756 with MTP); this V4.1 step also changes topology and HBM allocation. End to end, S0 -> S3 is 39x for Qwen3-8B (illustrative because S0 context is unverified; 4.0x is the modeled format step) and a modeled 8.9x for V4.1 at 1M; the steps are ordered by definition and S2-S3 are conditional on the design's open gates. The same roofline shows where ROM does not help: at 8K and a full batch, aggregate throughput is KV-bound on every machine, and the B200's eight stacks out-stream the ROM reticle's six (11,921 against 8,941 tok/s).
